findings.title: Exoneration separates the proved act from the self
findings.claim: The truth exposed, established, and spoken in 12:51 clears a concrete accusation, while 12:53's refusal to clear the self keeps that conduct-level verdict from becoming a certification of the person's whole nature.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier root_000099/B002 at 12:53:2:1 refuses clearance; the independent 12:50 inquiry and the 12:51 truth, reality, and truthful-speech carriers at 12:50:12, 12:51:21, 12:51:22, and 12:51:29 supply the preceding public test. Their contact changes exoneration from a general self-praise into a separation between a proved act and the person who remains accountable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold public vindication and inward vigilance together without treating either one as a verdict on the other.
findings.containment: This finding preserves the concrete truth of 12:51 and does not declare the self essentially corrupt or identify the 12:53 speaker with the 12:51 speaker as a settled fact. The relation is a bounded pericope reading.

epistemic.reason: The supplied channel nomination is trusted and every semantic member is anchored, but the cross-ayah synthesis remains an interpretive inference rather than a grammatical claim.

findings.title: Hidden betrayal meets guided inward government
findings.claim: The hidden breach and guidance of 12:52 meet the focus's inward command toward ugliness, mercy, and forgiveness, so effective inward government is imagined as a mercy-held response to susceptibility rather than as self-acquittal.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 12:53:6:2, 12:53:10:1, 12:53:7:3, 12:53:14:1, and 12:53:3:1/12:53:5:2 provide command, mercy, evil, protective forgiveness, and inward intention. The independent 12:52 carriers at 12:52:5, 12:52:6, and 12:52:10 provide breach, hiddenness, and gentle guidance. Their contact turns the focus from an isolated diagnosis into a local relation between concealed conduct, inner direction, and mercy-guided restraint.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the focus can name inward danger while still leaving room for a guided and merciful form of agency.
findings.containment: The finding remains inside the supplied 12:52-12:53 hinge. It does not name a surah-wide system, and it does not make guidance or mercy cancel the focus's plain assertion about the النفس.

They meet the focus carrier 12:53:6:2, where the registered authority facet names the self as an intensive commander toward سوء. The contact changes frequency of desire into a bounded jurisdictional analogy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish command as a neutral form from the question of which authority gives the command its binding direction.
findings.containment: The registered branch is used with its authority facet and the unbound judgment trace remains attributed. The focus is not declared a literal ruler, and the alternative that the sequence marks only recurrence and finality remains live.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT record is visible and its scope is complete, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound; the authority conflict is therefore retained as qualified inference.

findings.title: The self is a contested locus of allegiance
findings.claim: The repeated نفس constructions around 12:51-12:54 place the person between another's solicitation, the self's inward intention, and a later exclusive royal selection, so the focus's inner self can also be heard as a contested locus of allegiance.
findings.mechanism: The context carriers at 12:51:5 and 12:51:24 carry solicitation toward Yusuf's self, while 12:54:5 and 12:54:6 supply exclusive selection and its royal claimant. They meet the focus carriers 12:53:3:1 and 12:53:5:2, whose whole-self and inward-intention facets let the repeated possessors and prepositions contact one person-centered field. The changed reading is social as well as inward: desire, another person, and royal service make competing claims around the self.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus's نفس as a person situated among competing claims without losing its local inward meaning.
findings.containment: The social contest is an HFT-attributed inference from repeated constructions, not a new lexical gloss for نفس. The alternative that each pronoun remains local and the repetition only creates resonance stays visible.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies all coordinates and returns, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the contest of allegiance is an inference from the sequence.

The focus carrier 12:53:2:1 refuses self-clearance, while 12:53:14:1 carries both the registered protective-cover and moral-forgiveness facets. Their ordered contact changes the function of cover: it protects the person after accountability instead of making the underlying truth disappear.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear غَفُورٌ as protection that follows disclosure while keeping the focus's self-warning intact.
findings.containment: The focus's ordinary moral forgiveness remains primary. The physical-cover facet is retained as a contextual image, not as a replacement gloss, and no claim is made that the sequence proves a universal theology of concealment.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT sequence and focus branches are supplied, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the distinction between preserving cover and cover-up is an inference from order.

findings.title: Accountable vigilance can precede stewardship
findings.claim: The focus's refusal to certify the self is followed by trust, guarding, knowledge, enablement, and mercy, making non-exonerating vigilance perceptible as an internal safeguard that can accompany entrusted responsibility.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 12:53:2:1, 12:53:11:1/12:53:13:1, and 12:53:10:1/12:53:15:1 supply refused clearance, gradual completion, and divine mercy. The attributed context carriers at 12:54:14, 12:55:7, 12:55:8, and 12:56:2 supply trust, guarding, disclosed knowledge, and effective enablement. Their immediate sequence changes self-vigilance from disabling guilt into a possible safeguard for holding power, while mercy appears as the condition in which capacity is granted.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a path from moral self-scrutiny to trustworthy agency without turning self-scrutiny into a guarantee of perfection.
findings.containment: The stewardship relation is a qualified HFT inference from 12:53-12:56. The alternative that the narrative merely juxtaposes virtues remains live, and no causal doctrine beyond the supplied sequence is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies the ordered contacts, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the qualification-to-stewardship relation is inferred.

findings.title: Pressure and relief as an embodied analogy
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the prison and pressing images of 12:36 and 12:49 meet the focus branches for breath and relief, so harmful command can be pictured as pressured discharge from an enclosed interior while mercy opens room for a different response.
findings.mechanism: The attributed context carriers at 12:36:3, 12:36:9, and 12:49:11 supply confinement and pressing until extraction, while the focus carriers at 12:53:3:1/12:53:5:2 supply breath and relief from constriction. Their contact changes the moral sentence into an embodied analogy of interior pressure becoming outward directive and mercy creating release.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader gains a bodily picture for how an inward harmful command can emerge under pressure while keeping mercy as a real opening for response.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory analogy, not the lexical meaning of النفس or a claim that the focus describes a prison. The unbound context branches are attributed, and the ordinary moral reading remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT outlier is scope-complete but legacy_unbound and explicitly exploratory; the embodied mapping is retained with its stated boundary.

Their contact changes the scope of the focus's possessive Lord reference from an apparently private relation into personal access to a universal Lordship field.

The independent external triggers at 1:4:1 and 1:4:3 carry ownership or sovereignty and the day of accounting. Their contact changes the focus's rival-jurisdiction analogy by adding a bounded final standard against which inward command is measured.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the difference between an inward directive that seeks jurisdiction and the supplied image of authority over the final reckoning.
findings.containment: The overlay adds a local sovereignty frame to the focus authority image; it does not import all of 1:4-1:7 or claim that the focus itself describes judgment day.
